name: Meilisearch
tagline: A typo-tolerant search API you run yourself, without per-search billing.

local.note: Search only answers on this computer's localhost port, which is what you want for a personal app, and useless as a shared production API until you put it on a server.

quote.text: Only use the master key to manage API keys. Never use the master key to perform searches or other common operations.

citations.claim: The official Docker image exposes port 7700 and stores indexes under a configurable data path (/meili_data by default).
MEILI_MASTER_KEY must be set for a protected instance; without a master key, requests are not gated the way a public host requires.
At v1.52.0 the repository SPDX is MIT AND BUSL-1.1: parts of the tree are MIT and Meilisearch Enterprise Edition paths are under BUSL-1.1, not a separate product only.
MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS deactivates built-in telemetry when set.
Caddy obtains and renews TLS certificates automatically for any public hostname named in the Caddyfile.

whatYouSignUpFor: Source-available, not open source for the whole tree: SPDX at the pinned tag is MIT AND BUSL-1.1. Community Edition search is MIT; Enterprise Edition paths (sharding, S3-streaming snapshots and related EE work) are BUSL-1.1 and are not free to run in production without a commercial agreement. This install runs the published image and the MIT-covered search API you index against; it does not unlock EE-only features.
This is a search engine API, not a hosted dashboard product. You still write the code that indexes documents and queries them. There is no browser sign-in to finish.

You own the master key. Anyone with it can read and write every index and mint other keys; it is generated on the server and never pasted into a browser. Search clients get a search-scoped key from /keys.
You own disk growth. Indexes are not free, and a large crawl without retention planning will fill the volume.
High availability, multi-region analytics dashboards and managed ranking labs are not in this container. Those are what Algolia sells.
